---
title: "Probabilistic ML for Finance"
subtitle: "Master's short course · 10 hours · mixed backgrounds"
---

A 10-hour course for finance master's students from mixed backgrounds. The spine is
**dependence**: how to *measure* it (Module 1), estimate it in high dimensions
(Module 2), *propagate* it as risk (Module 3), and *remove* it for fairness
(Module 4). No ML background assumed — calculus and basic probability are enough.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Start Here
New to the data or the finance vocabulary (returns, crash, co-crash, VaR, beta)?
Begin with **[Markets for Data People](../../topics/data/index.qmd)** — a primer that
assumes you know data, not finance: every term is shown in the real data, with the
preprocessing laid bare, before any module uses it.
:::

## Three Ways In — Pick Your Depth

Every module comes in three forms; follow whichever you need:

- **Slides** — the lecture: ELI5, figure-driven, the big ideas in order.
- **Walkthrough** — the deep notes: full derivations, every figure reproducible.
- **Labs** — hands-on notebooks: build each tool, then run it on real market data.

## What Each Module Covers

**1 · Measures of dependence.** Two roads to a number for "do these move together?":
compare directly (Pearson → Spearman → distance correlation → HSIC) or go through the
density (entropy → mutual information → total correlation). The labs build each
measure on controlled data, then [hunt the hidden
risk](../../topics/dependence/labs/index.qmd) a correlation misses.

**2 · Gaussianization.** One invertible map that turns messy, dependent data into an
independent Gaussian — and runs *backward* to generate. Change of variables, RBIG,
and normalizing flows; the [labs](../../topics/gaussianization/labs/index.qmd) measure
mutual information in high dimensions and sample realistic scenarios.

**3 · Uncertainty.** Carry risk forward honestly: sample the *joint* (RBIG backward)
for portfolio VaR, and band a prediction with **predicted noise** (forecast
volatility) plus **ensembles** for model doubt. The
[labs](../../topics/uncertainty/labs/index.qmd) propagate a real portfolio to its tail
and calibrate a volatility interval.

**4 · Fair learning.** "Fair" = a prediction independent of a protected attribute —
the same dependence, now *removed*. Drop-and-leak, the CKA penalty, and adversarial
removal; the [labs](../../topics/fairness/labs/index.qmd) neutralize a credit model and
a market strategy.

## Format

- Concepts first on slides, then the deep walkthrough and hands-on labs for each module.
- Every figure on the slides is generated by code in this repo and can be reproduced live.
- Slides stay ELI5; the derivations, reproducible figures, and labs live in the matching
  [Topics](../../topics/dependence/index.qmd) pages.

## Demos

Live-coding notebooks live in `demos/` (Jupytext `.py`, paired to `.ipynb` on demand)
and **import** the course libraries — [rbig](https://github.com/jejjohnson/rbig),
[gauss_flows](https://github.com/jejjohnson/gauss_flows),
[pyrox](https://github.com/jejjohnson/pyrox), and
[keras-fairkl](https://github.com/jejjohnson/keras-fairkl) — rather than copying them,
so the maths stays in the Topics pages. Module 1's demo is live; the rest are in
progress.
